extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications providers, small businesses, auction participants, and regulatory/industry analysts preparing comments or compliance assessments for FCC rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Identification and application of SBA/NAICS small business size standards and FCC auction-designated-entity definitions across categories of wireline, wireless, and other telecommunications providers, as used in the FCC's regulatory and regulatory-flexibility analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Service Providers (Non-Broadband) small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for this industry classifies firms with annual receipts of $35 million or less as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to ISPs using client-supplied telecommunications connections (e.g., dial-up ISPs) and VoIP providers using client-supplied connections (NAICS: All Other Telecommunications). U.S. Census Bureau 2017 data show 1,079 firms in this industry that operated for the entire year; 1,039 had revenue of less than $25 million, so a majority can be considered small. (See footnotes/citations to NAICS definitions and Census data.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Wired Telecommunications Carriers small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for Wired Telecommunications Carriers classifies firms having 1,500 or fewer employees as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines establishments operating/ providing access to owned/leased wired transmission facilities (services include wired telephony, VoIP, cable audio/video distribution, wired broadband). 2017 Census data: 3,054 firms operated for the entire year; 2,964 had fewer than 250 employees. Commission data (2021) identify 4,590 providers reporting fixed local services; estimated 4,146 have 1,500 or fewer employees; consequently most can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Exchange Carriers (LECs) size classification (use Wired Telecommunications Carriers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the Commission nor the SBA has a size standard specific to local exchange services; Wired Telecommunications Carriers is the closest industry with an SBA small business size standard of 1,500 or fewer employees for small-business classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers include incumbent and competitive local exchange providers; Census/Commission data cited (3,054 firms in Wired Telecoms; Commission estimates 4,146 fixed local exchange service providers with 1,500 or fewer employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incumbent Local Exchange Carriers (Incumbent LECs) size classification
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific small-business size standard exists for incumbent LECs; apply the Wired Telecommunications Carriers SBA standard (1,500 or fewer employees) to estimate small-entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census Bureau and Commission Universal Service Monitoring Report data used to estimate counts (e.g., 1,212 providers reporting incumbent LEC status; Commission estimates 916 have 1,500 or fewer employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Local Exchange Carriers (CLECs) size classification
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific small-business size standard exists for competitive LECs; apply the Wired Telecommunications Carriers SBA standard (1,500 or fewer employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census and Commission data: 3,378 providers reporting competitive local exchange service; Commission estimates 3,230 have 1,500 or fewer employees; therefore most can be considered small under SBA standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interexchange Carriers (IXCs) size classification
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific small-business size standard exists for interexchange carriers; Wired Telecommunications Carriers (1,500 or fewer employees) is used as the closest SBA standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data and Commission estimates (127 providers reporting interexchange services; Commission estimates 109 have 1,500 or fewer employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator Service Providers (OSPs) size classification
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific SBA size standard exists for operator service providers; apply Wired Telecommunications Carriers standard (1,500 or fewer employees) for small-business classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data context: 20 providers reported providing operator services; Commission estimates all 20 have 1,500 or fewer employees; thus all can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Toll Carriers size classification
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific SBA size standard exists for Other Toll Carriers; use Wired Telecommunications Carriers SBA standard (1,500 or fewer employees) as closest applicable standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category includes toll carriers not classified as IXCs, OSPs, prepaid calling card providers, satellite carriers, or toll resellers. Commission data: 90 providers reported other toll services; Commission estimates 87 have 1,500 or fewer employees; most can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite) small business size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA size standard for this industry classifies a business as small if it has 1,500 or fewer employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry comprises establishments operating/maintaining switching and transmission facilities for airwave communications (cellular, paging, wireless Internet, wireless video). 2017 Census data: 2,893 firms; 2,837 employed fewer than 250. Commission (2021) data: 594 providers reported wireless services; Commission estimates 511 have 1,500 or fewer employees; most can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless Communications Services (WCS) small-entity and auction eligibility guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite) is the closest industry with SBA small business size standard (1,500 or fewer employees) applicable to WCS licensees; auction bidding credits/installment-payment eligibility may be available to several types of small businesses defined by average gross revenues (small, very small, entrepreneur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WCS can be used for fixed, mobile, radiolocation, and digital audio broadcasting satellite services; licensed under Part 27. When bidding credits are adopted for WCS auctions, credits may be available pursuant to competitive bidding rules and designated-entity sections in Part 27 (Subparts D–Q contain band-specific small business size standards). The Commission does not generally track subsequent business size after auctions unless assignments/transfers/unjust enrichment issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated-entity definitions in auctions (general auction small-business mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: In frequency bands subject to auction, the Commission may adopt bidding credits and installment payment options that provide preferential treatment to entities classified as small, very small, or entrepreneur, based on average gross revenues and designated-entity rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific small-business definitions for auctions vary by frequency band and are set forth in competitive bidding rules and in designated-entity sections (e.g., Part 27 Subparts D–Q). The number of winning bidders qualifying as small at auction close does not necessarily equal the number of small businesses in service; the Commission does not routinely track subsequent business size unless required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1670–1675 MHz service auction small/very-small business definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 1670–1675 MHz service band auctions, a 'small business' is defined as an entity that, together with affiliates and controlling interests, has average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years, and a 'very small business' is defined as an entity that ... has average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions apply to bidding credit/installment-payment eligibility for licenses in the 1670–1675 MHz band (see 47 CFR § 27.906(a)). Commission data (Nov 2021) show three active licenses in the band; the winning bidder in the referenced auction did not claim small-business status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband PCS auction small/very-small business definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In auctions for Broadband PCS licenses, the Commission defined 'small business' as an entity that, together with affiliates and controlling interests, has average gross revenues not exceeding $40 million for the preceding three years, and 'very small business' as average annual gross revenues not exceeding $15 million for the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These auction-size thresholds were applied for winning bidders claiming small-business credits in Broadband PCS C, D, E, and F Blocks. Commission data (Nov 2021) indicated approximately 5,060 active Broadband PCS licenses; winning-bidder claims at auction do not necessarily reflect current in-service small-entity counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless telephony small-entity classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireless telephony (cellular, PCS, specialized mobile radio telephony carriers) is assessed using the Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite) SBA small business size standard (1,500 or fewer employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data: 2,893 firms in industry; Commission (2021) data: 331 providers reported provision of cellular/PCS/SMR services; Commission estimates 255 have 1,500 or fewer employees; consequently most can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized Mobile Radio (SMR) licenses small-entity classification
rubrics_metrics.description: SMR licensees are evaluated using the Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite) SBA size standard (1,500 or fewer employees) as the closest applicable size standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMR licenses permit commercial land mobile communications in 800/900 MHz bands for voice/data/paging/fax, etc. Commission data (2021) reported 95 SMR (dispatch) providers; Commission estimates all 95 have 1,500 or fewer employees. There were 3,924 active SMR licenses (Dec 2021), but employee counts are not collected so the Commission cannot precisely estimate how many licensees meet SBA thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission data and tracking limitations relevant to small-entity estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission does not generally track subsequent business size after auctions unless assignments/transfers or unjust enrichment issues arise; it does not collect employee counts for licensees providing many services, limiting its ability to estimate how many active licensees qualify as small under SBA standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: the number of winning bidders that claim small-business status at auction close does not necessarily represent the number of small businesses in service. Where employee counts or revenues are lacking, the Commission uses closest-available NAICS categories and available Census/Commission reports to estimate small-entity prevalence, and notes uncertainty in estimates.
